title: Review of "Public Servant" Definition in Penal Code and Singapore's Anti-corruption Laws following Conviction of Former Minister
what_it_is: Review of "Public Servant" Definition in Penal Code and Singapore's Anti-corruption Laws following Conviction of Former Minister

sections.label: Corruption case and public confidence
sections.summary: Questions ask about the public impact of the former Trade Relations Minister's case and whether anti-corruption laws and the Penal Code's public servant definition should be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) what is his assessment of the public impact of the case involving the former Minister-in-charge of Trade Relations on building public confidence in a culture of zero tolerance for corruption among Government officials; and (b) whether Singapore’s anti-corruption laws should be reviewed for greater efficacy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance whether the definition of "public servant" under the Penal Code is fit for purpose for an offence under section 165 of the Penal Code.

sections.label: Section 165 as anti-corruption lever
sections.summary: Section 165 of the Penal Code is one legislative lever within a wider system of checks and balances against public sector corruption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Section 165 of the Penal Code is one of the legislative levers that are part of the wider system of checks and balances to combat corruption in the public sector.

sections.label: Reviewing Penal Code provisions transfer
sections.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs is still reviewing whether and how to port certain Chapter 9 Penal Code provisions to the Prevention of Corruption Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Ministry of Home Affairs is still reviewing whether and, if so, how, to port over certain provisions of Chapter 9 of the Penal Code to the Prevention of Corruption Act (PCA).

sections.label: Decisive action over rule changes
sections.summary: Where clear rules are flouted or ignored, the response should be decisive action against the offender, not adjusting the rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If the rules were clear, but were flouted or ignored, what we need to do is not to adjust the rules, but to take decisive action against the offender.

sections.label: Multi-pronged integrity effort
sections.summary: Maintaining the integrity of the system is a multi-pronged and continuous effort, as explained to the House in February 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: As I explained to Members of this House in February 2024, maintaining the integrity of our system is a multi-pronged and continuous effort.

sections.label: Audits and anti-corruption institutions
sections.summary: System-level measures include regular internal and external audits and institutions like the Auditor-General's Office and CPIB to address issues other checks miss.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: At the system level, we must have regular internal audits, external audits and have institutions like the Auditor-General's Office and Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau (CPIB) to respond to issues not picked up by other layers of checks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The recent developments show that we do not shy away from doing the right thing to uphold the trust that Singaporeans have in the Government and this is what we will continue to do.

sections.label: Charges reduced to non-corruption
sections.summary: The passage states that charges against a former Minister were reduced to non-corruption cases on the trial's first day.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The first question is, we all remember the damaging headlines in the middle of last year and how the former Minister was subsequently barred from Government buildings and charged under the PCA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But on the first day of the trial in September, the charges were suddenly reduced to non-corruption cases.

sections.label: Judge imposed double sentence
sections.summary: The passage states that at sentencing the Judge imposed imprisonment double what the Prosecution had asked for.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, at the sentencing stage of the case, the Judge decided to impose a sentence of imprisonment that was double what the Prosecution had asked for.

sections.label: Aligning section 165 with PCA
sections.summary: The passage states Minister Shanmugam previously raised whether section 165 needs alignment with the PCA in a different formulation.

sentences.text: My second set of comments on the PCA review, I think Minister Shanmugam has also said this before as to whether and if there is a need for us to align the section 165 with the PCA in a different formulation, that we can consider.

sections.label: Section 165 is corruption charge
sections.summary: The passage states that section 165 is a corruption charge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, on the second point, section 165 is a corruption charge.

sections.label: Belief they did job properly
sections.summary: The passage states there are reasons to believe they have done their job properly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Yes, we have reasons to believe that they have done their job properly.
